data.hook: Boise State trailed 17-3 at halftime, then unleashed a dominant ground game to flip the script. But a controversial fumble call on a muffed punt stole the spotlight, leaving Memphis fans fuming.
data.name: Boise State Rallies Past Memphis 38-20 Amid Officiating Firestorm
data.summary: The Broncos stormed back behind Dylan Riley's 206 rushing yards, outscoring Memphis 35-3 after the break for a 38-20 win at Albertsons Stadium. The turning point came on a second-half punt where officials awarded Boise State a recovery despite video evidence many said showed Memphis had possession cleanly, with no replay review. Memphis coach Charles Huff pointed to red-zone issues in his postgame comments, while the call drew sharp criticism from Tigers supporters and analysts labeling it among the worst they've seen. The victory boosts Boise State's playoff hopes, but the officiating talk overshadowed the rally.

data.hook: Ralphie the bison charged onto Folsom Field with such power that her four handlers could barely keep up, setting an explosive tone for Colorado's home opener.
data.name: Buffaloes Crush Weber State 52-21 Behind Lewis's Record First Half
data.summary: The Colorado Buffaloes improved to 2-0 with a dominant 52-21 win over Weber State, fueled by freshman quarterback Julian Lewis's school-record 212 passing yards in the first quarter alone. Lewis finished 17 of 23 for 366 yards, four passing touchdowns, a rushing score, and no picks, including long bombs of 66 and 63 yards right out of the gate. Ralphie's pregame sprint thrilled the sold-out crowd under clear skies, while running back Micah Welch added 106 yards and a 55-yard touchdown. Coach Deion Sanders reminded everyone there's still work to do as the team builds momentum.

data.hook: Western Michigan fans packed Waldo Stadium, cheering as their Broncos dominated Monmouth 49-14 for the season's first win and a big confidence boost.
data.name: Western Michigan Broncos Crush Monmouth 49-14 in Home Opener
data.summary: Broc Lowry threw three touchdown passes and Jalen Buckley ran for three scores, leading the Broncos to a 21-0 halftime lead and a runaway victory before 24,605 fans—the largest home opener crowd since 2017. Backup QB Trey Petty hit Ryan Brotherton for his first career touchdown in the fourth quarter, while the defense forced turnovers. The win followed last week's controversial 13-12 loss at Michigan, showcasing the team's resilience as they head to face Rice next.

data.hook: Rookie Kahlil Benson steps into the spotlight, set to protect Patrick Mahomes on his NFL debut against Denver's fierce pass rush.
data.name: Chiefs Rule Out Simmons and Conner for Broncos Opener
data.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs will miss left tackle Josh Simmons, sidelined by a back injury, and safety Chamarri Conner for Monday's season opener against the Denver Broncos at Arrowhead Stadium. Undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson, who impressed in training camp, makes his debut at left tackle, with Jaylon Moore starting at right tackle. Coach Andy Reid expressed optimism about the depth options, while defensive star Chris Jones is good to go despite a minor calf issue. The Broncos arrive fully healthy, setting up a tough test for Mahomes in his return from last season's ACL injury.

data.hook: Brock Bowers, the Raiders' dynamic tight end, got a meniscus trim on his knee and will sit out Sunday's opener against Miami. The team hopes he'll be back the following week at the Chargers.
data.name: Raiders' Brock Bowers Out for Opener After Knee Procedure, Eye Week 2 Return
data.summary: The 23-year-old star had the minor procedure Tuesday after dealing with the knee issue since training camp. Backup Michael Mayer steps in for Week 1, fresh off a new contract and added bulk for the role. While the Raiders stay optimistic, fans and medical experts urge caution given Bowers' past knee injuries from last season and typical three-to-six week recoveries—many simply say 'LET HIM HEAL' to avoid risks.

data.hook: Ashton Jeanty's ready to run, but Brock Bowers' knee procedure sidelines the Raiders' star tight end just before kickoff.
data.name: Raiders Get Jeanty Back but Rule Out Bowers for Dolphins Opener
data.summary: The Las Vegas Raiders cleared running back Ashton Jeanty from the injury report after his ankle recovery, setting him up for a full workload in Sunday's 4:25 p.m. ET home opener against the Miami Dolphins at Allegiant Stadium. Star tight end Brock Bowers, however, is out following a Tuesday meniscus trim, with a possible Week 2 return against the Chargers. Both rebuild-mode teams start new head coaches and QBs—Kirk Cousins for Vegas under Klint Kubiak, Malik Willis for Miami with Jeff Hafley—while Dolphins are mostly healthy and former QB Ryan Fitzpatrick warns of a potential 0-17 season.
